outcome: Neither sub-question has been settled: the decidability of the elementary theory of Z_p((t)) (Laurent series over the p-adic integers) and of the field of rational functions/polynomials over C (i.e. full first-order Th(C(t))) both remain open as of September 2026.
summary: The Wikipedia bullet actually poses two separate decidability questions with no attached citation in the frozen revision: (1) is the elementary theory of Z_p((t)) — Laurent series over the p-adic integers, a mixed-characteristic henselian valued field — decidable, and (2) is the elementary theory of the field of rational functions/polynomials over C decidable. I confirmed the exact wikitext via the frozen revision's raw text and found no footnote pinning either sub-question to a specific source, consistent with these being long-standing folklore open problems in the model theory of valued fields (in the tradition of Ax-Kochen-Ershov). I checked the most promising leads flagged by triage: Kuhlmann's December 2025 survey 'Model theory of tame valued fields and beyond' (arXiv:2512.06386), which lists 16 open problems but, on direct query of its content, does not discuss Z_p((t)) or C(t)/C[t] decidability at all — it focuses on tame, perfectoid and deeply ramified fields in equicharacteristic and mixed characteristic, not on this specific pair of questions. Scanlon's August 2025 paper on 'complicated structures definable in C(t)' addresses definable substructures of C(t), not the decidability of the full first-order theory of C(t) itself, and does not claim to resolve it. Kartas's work (2020's 'Decidability via the tilting correspondence', predating the window, and follow-ups through 2025) makes substantial progress on decidability of various p-adic and perfectoid fields via tilting/perfectoid-transfer techniques, and Anscombe-Fehm's 'Universal-existential theories of fields' (2024, arXiv:2405.12771) studies universal-existential fragments and reductions between theories of function fields and Laurent series fields — but neither claims to resolve the full elementary theory of Z_p((t)) itself, nor of C(t)/C[t]. General web searches on Hilbert's Tenth Problem for C(t) (the closely related existential/Diophantine question) confirm the single-variable case remains explicitly unresolved and is described in the literature as 'the most annoying piece of our ignorance in the area' — only the multivariable case C(t1,t2) was resolved (Kim-Roush, 1992, well before the window). No source found any claim, partial or full, of a resolution to either sub-question inside the 26 Jan 2024–Sep 2026 window, and no AI system appears anywhere in this niche area of model theory research.
competing_reading: One could argue that Kartas's perfectoid-transfer program and the Anscombe-Fehm reductions constitute 'progress' in a loose sense, since they resolve decidability for structurally adjacent fields (F_p((t)) and its perfect/perfectoid variants, Q_p(zeta_{p^infty}), Q_p(p^{1/p^infty})) using techniques that could plausibly one day bear on Z_p((t)) itself. But per §3.1, a related/adjacent field is a different question, not a restriction of the stated one, and none of these papers claim their results imply anything about Z_p((t)) or C(t) decidability directly — so I did not code this as `partial` or `progress`. If a paper is found stating an explicit corollary for Z_p((t)) itself, this should be revisited.
what_would_settle_it: A paper (or the next edition of Kuhlmann's survey, or a future update to the Wikipedia article's own footnotes) that explicitly states a decidability or undecidability result for the full elementary theory of Z_p((t)) or of C(t)/C[t], with a proof or a clear statement that it remains open with attribution to a specific researcher.
